differences.what: massing: the draft's generic block is now the photograph's: a light stone front two storeys over a raised basement, its corona at about 11.7 m and the mansard's curb near 15.7 m; the front's north corner, the cornice along it and both street dormers lie within about 10-15 px of the print's

the canted bay at the front's south end, carried through both storeys and up through the cornice under its own slated crown with a cresting, a light in each face on each storey at the front's heights, where the print has it (x 470-690 px)

the porch on columns at the stoop's head, its entablature about 5.7-6.35 m and a balcony on it before the window over the door; the terrace along the front at the principal floor north of the stoop; the broad stoop
three opening columns north of the bay (the door's and two windows'), the chamber windows over the principal ones, each window under a hood
the deep cornice on paired brackets over a frieze, turned round the bay and along the south flank
the slated mansard with two dormers on its street face (over the door's column and between the two northern columns) and one on its south face
a low coped stone wall before the lawn, broken by the walk before the stoop, in place of the draft's fence

every street window ROUND-HEADED under a moulded hood with a carved crown (the print; the mid-century and 2024 fronts and the c. 2014 detail show the same heads on both storeys): T-3208 cuts each front light round-headed in the stone (street_front_round_heads), K06's arch band carried spring to spring as the hood and a key block on its crown for the carving, and the corner bay's lights the same; they render on the print's columns and crowns

the window over the porch is a PAIRED, arched window (two round lights under one wider head, about 1.25 m across; the c. 2014 detail and the 2024 front show it plainly); since T-3208 it is round-headed like its neighbours but still ONE light of the front's width, because a front laid by front_bays glazes every column with one K06 variant and K01's round-hooded light is a single sash

the south flank's front part is the same light STONE as the front in the print (the mid-century oblique, a print of the same negative, agrees; no later picture shows the flank); the build lays it in K03 brick, because the 1911 sheet records 'brick with stone front' and K01 returns stone along a flank only as a quoined return of at most 4 m, where the print shows about 6 m of flank and no quoins. Its windows there are square-headed, where the print's are round-headed under hoods
the dormers' heads ARCHED: T-3208 builds all three as K05's round-headed dormer, the surround carried round the arch, where the gable heads stood; they render on the print's dormers

the bay's crown carries a DORMER on its front face (the print's x 600-680 px; the mid-century and 2024 fronts and the c. 2014 detail show it as an arched light under its own cornice); K08's mansard crown takes none, and nothing in the kit sets a dormer on a bay's roof
the porch's columns are a pair a side with responds and the balcony's rail stands about 0.5 m higher than built (0.35 m, the most K01's hood leaves under the window's sill) — T-3208
the terrace stands on carved brackets over the basement with its basement lights between them, and a low rail on it; built as a solid stone terrace — T-3208

the square stone posts at the walk's opening and at the lot's front corners: T-3208 raises the coping wall there to about 0.8 m for about 0.45-0.5 m (they render at the print's x 520-530 and 720-735 beside the walk); the stoop's two block newels at its foot (the print, the mid-century and 2024 fronts) are not built — see the next item

the stoop's two square block newels at its foot, about 1.2 m high with carved caps (the print's x 600 and 700; the mid-century and 2024 fronts), and its iron hand-rails: the build's stoop has solid stone cheeks and no newels. K11's coping wall stands one stair pier on one side only and K07's balustrade would add balusters no picture shows
the bay's crown reads a little higher and broader in the print, whose top edge cuts it at about 15.3 m; built 4.0 m over its eaves

the corona over the bay reads about 1 m higher in the print than in the render at the bay's south cheek (y 181 against about 240 px), where the camera's fit and the 1911 sheet's bay disagree (the sheet bulges 1.8 m at v 2.0-6.1, the print 0.93 m at v 0.3-4.3). Weighed against the mid-century and 2024 fronts: in both the bay's cornice runs level with the front's (the brackets and the corona continue round the bay unbroken), which is how it is built, so the difference is the camera's fit at the bay's corner rather than the cornice; it stays open until a camera solved on a front confirms it, since a re-fit is not this sign-off's
colour and the stone's tone: the print is monochrome sepia
the north flank, the rear and the sheet's frame range behind: the print does not see them; the south flank's canted bay stands behind the neighbour at the print's left

the hoods' carving and the window surrounds: the pictures show each hood's crown as a foliate cartouche and a moulded architrave down each jamb on consoles; built as the arch band and a plain key block, without the jamb mouldings. Under 0.15 m proud and a carving's detail: within tolerance

the round-headed lights' glazing: the c. 2014 detail shows each upper sash following the arch; K06's round-headed hung sash puts a transom bar on the spring under a fanlight. A glazing bar: within tolerance
the coping wall's posts are the wall's 0.35 m thickness where the print's are a little broader (about 0.5 m): under the bar, within tolerance

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153).
